students' perceptions of corporate social responsibility.

how students perceive corporate social responsibility and whether these perceptions are related to student characteristics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

CSR is a concept that is not well defined, but is generally accepted to be the responsibility of a company to act as a good corporate citizen, and to take responsibility for the impact of its activities on the environment, the community, its employees and the general public.

CSR is a business approach to create long-term shareholder value by "embracing responsibility for the firm's effects on society" (Orlitzky and Benjamin, 2001, 2001; see also Carroll, 1979; Donaldson and Preston, 1995; Freeman, 1994; McWilliams and Siegel 2000; 2001; 2006; Porter and Kramer, 2006; and Wood, 1991).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CSR concept is a complex one and that there is no one definition of CSR.
CSR is a very important topic and that there are many aspects to consider when implementing CSR in a company.
CSR is a key element in today's Business school curriculum and is a key component of tomorrow's business leaders' worldviews.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no single way to measure social impact.
the business school is not the only institution that can teach students about CSR, and that students are already exposed to CSR in other ways.

the more you can get students to think critically and to think about the ethical implications of their actions, the more they will do so, the better they'll do in class, and the more they will be able to apply that thinking to the real world.
